spec.description: Per-guest CPU, memory, disk and network for QEMU VMs and LXC containers, including PSI pressure stalls. Power state is derived from uptime -- Proxmox emits no status metric.

spec.expr: count(proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} > 0) or (count(proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"}) * 0)

spec.title: Stopped
spec.description: Includes templates, which are permanently stopped and indistinguishable from a genuinely down guest -- Proxmox emits no template flag.

spec.expr: count(proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} == 0) or (count(proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"}) * 0)

spec.title: By Type
spec.description: Guest count split by virtualisation type.

spec.title: vCPU Allocated
spec.description: Sum of vCPUs across running guests. Compare with the node's physical core count on the Node dashboard.

spec.expr: sum(proxmox_vm_cpus{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} and proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} > 0) or (count(proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"}) * 0)

spec.title: RAM Allocated
spec.description: RAM promised to running guests.

spec.expr: sum(proxmox_vm_maxmem{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} and proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} > 0) or (count(proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"}) * 0)

spec.title: Disk Provisioned
spec.description: Total provisioned virtual disk across all guests, running or not. Actual consumption on the storage is usually lower (thin provisioning).

spec.title: Power State
spec.description: Running vs stopped over time. Bands merge, so this shows the duration of each state rather than individual samples.

spec.title: Guest Inventory
spec.description: Every guest in scope. CPU and memory columns are meaningless for stopped guests -- they report 0.

spec.expr: sum by (vmid, name, type, node) (proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"})
sum by (vmid, name, type, node) (proxmox_vm_cpu{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"})
sum by (vmid, name, type, node) (proxmox_vm_cpus{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"})
sum by (vmid, name, type, node) (proxmox_vm_mem{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} / proxmox_vm_maxmem{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"})
sum by (vmid, name, type, node) (proxmox_vm_maxmem{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"})
sum by (vmid, name, type, node) (proxmox_vm_maxdisk{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"})

spec.title: CPU per Guest
spec.description: Fraction of the guest's OWN vCPUs in use -- 1.0 means the guest is saturating everything it was given, not the whole node.

spec.expr: proxmox_vm_cpu{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} and proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} > 0
topk(10, proxmox_vm_cpu{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} and proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} > 0)

spec.title: CPU Pressure (some)
spec.description: PSI: share of time at least one task was stalled waiting for CPU. Emitted only for running guests.

spec.title: CPU Pressure (full)
spec.description: PSI: share of time EVERY task was stalled on CPU. This is real lost work, and the more actionable of the two.

spec.title: Memory per Guest
spec.description: Used share of each guest's assigned RAM.

spec.expr: (proxmox_vm_mem{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} / proxmox_vm_maxmem{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"}) and proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} > 0

topk(10, (proxmox_vm_mem{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} / proxmox_vm_maxmem{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"}) and proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} > 0)

spec.title: Memory Pressure (full)
spec.description: PSI memory stall. Non-zero here means the guest is thrashing.

spec.title: LXC Swap
spec.description: Containers only -- QEMU guests manage swap inside the VM and never report it here.

spec.expr: (proxmox_vm_swap{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} / proxmox_vm_maxswap{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"}) and proxmox_vm_uptime{node=~"$node", type=~"$type", vmid=~"$guest"} > 0

options.content: The panels below come from the QEMU **balloon driver**, which reports what the guest OS sees rather than what the host allocated. They exist only for QEMU guests with the driver loaded — LXC containers and driverless VMs report nothing here, which is why each panel names that case explicitly instead of drawing an empty graph.

spec.title: Balloon Reclaim
spec.description: How much RAM the balloon driver is currently holding back from the guest: the gap between what the host granted (actual) and what the guest OS can see (total_mem). A rising line means the host is quietly taking memory back, which the guest experiences as shrinking capacity long before any pressure metric moves.

defaults.noValue: No QEMU guest reporting a balloon driver

spec.title: Guest Page Faults
spec.description: Major faults hit backing storage; minor faults are served from RAM. Minor faults are ordinary and scale with activity. It is a sustained MAJOR fault rate that matters -- it means the guest's working set no longer fits and it is paging against its disk.

defaults.noValue: No QEMU guest reporting a balloon driver

spec.title: Guest-Internal Swap
spec.description: Swap activity INSIDE the VM, which the host cannot otherwise see -- proxmox_vm_swap covers containers only. A VM can be swapping heavily while its host-side memory usage looks calm, and this is the only panel that shows it.

defaults.noValue: No QEMU guest reporting a balloon driver

spec.title: Disk Throughput
spec.description: Guest disk I/O. Writes negated so the directions mirror. Matches the sum of the per-disk blockstat counters below.

spec.title: I/O Pressure (full)
spec.description: PSI I/O stall -- the guest-side symptom of a slow or contended storage backend.

options.content: Proxmox bakes the virtual disk name into the **metric name** (`proxmox_vm_blockstat_scsi0_rd_bytes_total`) instead of using a label, so the two panels below match on `__name__` and rebuild a `disk` label with `label_replace`. QEMU guests only — LXC containers have no block device layer here.

spec.title: Per-Disk Throughput
spec.description: Combined read + write bandwidth for the six busiest QEMU virtual disks.

spec.title: Per-Guest I/O Latency
spec.description: Average service time per I/O operation, from the QEMU block layer's own accounting (total_time_ns / operations). The single best indicator that storage is the bottleneck.

spec.title: Per-Disk IOPS
spec.description: Operations per second per virtual disk, writes negated so the directions mirror. Throughput and IOPS answer different questions: a disk can be saturated on small random operations while its byte rate still looks modest, and only this panel shows that.

spec.title: Failed I/O Operations
spec.description: Read, write, and flush operations the QEMU block layer reported as FAILED. On healthy storage this is a flat zero line -- and a flat zero drawn here is the point: it distinguishes 'storage is fine' from 'the panel has no data', which an empty graph cannot do. Any departure from zero is a hardware or backend fault, not a performance symptom.

spec.expr: sum by (vmid,disk) (rate(label_replace({__name__=~"proxmox_vm_blockstat_[a-z0-9]+_failed_rd_operations_total"}, "disk", "$1", "__name__", "proxmox_vm_blockstat_([a-z0-9]+)_failed_rd_operations_total")[$__rate_interval])) + sum by (vmid,disk) (rate(label_replace({__name__=~"proxmox_vm_blockstat_[a-z0-9]+_failed_wr_operations_total"}, "disk", "$1", "__name__", "proxmox_vm_blockstat_([a-z0-9]+)_failed_wr_operations_total")[$__rate_interval])) + sum by (vmid,disk) (rate(label_replace({__name__=~"proxmox_vm_blockstat_[a-z0-9]+_failed_flush_operations_total"}, "disk", "$1", "__name__", "proxmox_vm_blockstat_([a-z0-9]+)_failed_flush_operations_total")[$__rate_interval]))

spec.title: fsync Latency
spec.description: How long a flush-to-stable-storage takes, from the QEMU block layer's own accounting. This is the number databases actually live or die on -- Postgres, etcd, and Elasticsearch all commit synchronously, so their throughput is bounded by this latency and not by the read/write bandwidth on the panels above. A guest can look idle on every other panel while fsync latency quietly makes it unusable.

spec.title: I/O Workload Fingerprint
spec.description: Each virtual disk placed by the SHAPE of its traffic rather than its volume: average request size on the horizontal, operations per second on the vertical, bubble sized by raw throughput. Large-and-slow at the right is sequential bulk work; small-and-fast at the top left is random or metadata-heavy work that will be latency-bound. Two disks on the same host routinely land in opposite corners, and that difference decides which one benefits from faster storage. `label_join` builds a single vmid·disk key because joinByField can only match on one field.

spec.title: Thin-Provision High-Water Mark
spec.description: The highest byte offset each virtual disk has EVER been written to. On thin-provisioned storage this is the floor the volume can never shrink below without discard, no matter how much the guest deletes -- a disk whose high-water mark has reached its provisioned size is permanently fully allocated on the backend. Read it together with the discard panel: TRIM is the only thing that moves real usage back down.

spec.title: Discard / TRIM Rate
spec.description: Bytes per second the guest is handing back to the storage backend via discard. This is the only mechanism that returns space from a thin volume after the high-water mark above has been set. A flat zero on a guest that deletes data means discard is not reaching the backend -- check that the disk has `discard=on` and that the guest filesystem issues TRIM. Space will otherwise be consumed permanently.

spec.title: Fleet Network Throughput
spec.description: Fleet-wide inbound and outbound throughput. Outbound is negated so the directions mirror; the panel below identifies the busiest guests.

spec.title: Top Talkers
spec.description: Combined in + out. Flat colour -- busiest is not worst.

spec.title: Cumulative Transfer
spec.description: Fleet-wide inbound and outbound bytes per display interval -- useful for spotting bulk transfers that a rate chart smooths away. Per-guest rankings are above.

spec.title: Proxmox VE · Guests (VM & LXC)
